newsitem.title: USA: Texaco combines gas, power activities.
newsitem.headline: Texaco combines gas, power activities.

text.p: Texaco Inc has combined two natural gas marketing operations with its alternate energy department to form Texaco Global Gas and Power, the company said Wednesday.

The new organization, which Texaco calls GG&P, will to manage its worldwide natural gas, natural gas liquids, electric power and synthesis gas marketing and project development activities, combining the activities of Texaco Natural Gas North America; Texaco Natural Gas International and Texaco's Alternate Energy Department.

Stating "Texaco is already a recognized leader in natural gas marketing, private power development and gasification," Glenn F. Tilton, Texaco's Senior Vice President and President, Global Businesses, said "by operating in the global marketplace with a single voice, we can more effectively provide efficient and environmentally smart energy solutions for our customers."
The company said Texaco Natural Gas - North America will continue the functions of the former North American unit while international activities will be covered by two new units.
One new unit, International Marketing and Business Development will be headed by Graham H. Batcheler, now general manager of Texaco's Gas Department, the company said.

The unit is responsible for commercializing Texaco's gas reserves, for wholesale and retail gas marketing in mature, deregulated countries like the United Kingdom, and for the development of gas to liquid conversion processes. The group will also develop new market-driven midstream and downstream opportunities that utilize Texaco's power, natural gas and gasification competencies.

As new international businesses are initiated it will become the responsibility of another new unit, GG&P's Project Development and Operations team, headed by James C. Houck, now general manager of the company's Alternate Energy Group.

The team will handle for further development, including bid submissions, contract negotiations, engineering, financing, construction and operations. Existing power generation operations and commercialization of Texaco's proprietary gasification technology are also the responsibility of this unit, Texaco said.

Texaco Natural Gas - North America, headed by Terry Hudgens, markets more than 3.3 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 325,000 barrels of natural gas liquids daily. It is responsible for the Texaco Star Center, a gas marketing and services business that operates gas processing plants, intrastate pipelines and natural gas storage facilities.

It also runs Texaco's Natural Gas Liquids business, engaged in worldwide product trading, wholesale propane marketing, and global ship chartering. The unit also includes the interstate Sabine Pipe Line Co.

Worldwide, Texaco and its partners operate private power facilities that produce more than 2,000 megawatts of power for internal use and for sale to utilities, the company said. The facilities also provide steam and thermal energy for enhanced oil recovery projects, refineries and manufacturing processes.
Additional projects under development include a 700-megawatt gas-fired plant in Thailand and a 300-megawatt oil-fueled cogeneration facility in the Philippines.
Texaco's gasification technology is also licensed for projects operating or under development in the U.S., Europe and Asia to provide syngas for the power, chemicals and refining industries.
